blocks.text: Creda is a digital platform that connects food suppliers with commercial buyers in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. It lets them complete orders with immediate or deferred payment, follow up on receivables and collection, and view credit indicators based on payment behavior within the platform.

The platform is operated by Creda Solutions Trading Company Limited (“we”). We respect your privacy and are committed to protecting your personal data in accordance with the Personal Data Protection Law and its implementing regulations in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

This Policy explains the data we collect, the purpose of collecting it, how we collect, store, process and destroy it, the parties we share it with, and your rights and how to exercise them. We make this Policy available to you before collecting your data, and we ask you to review it when creating your account.

Personal data in this Policy means any data that identifies you specifically, or makes it possible to identify you directly or indirectly, including: name, ID number, addresses, contact numbers, registration and license numbers, photos, and any financial or credit data related to you.

We collect only the minimum personal data necessary to achieve the purposes described in this Policy. We collect only the data you provide yourself, data generated by your use of the platform, data provided by the users you deal with, or data we obtain from official verification bodies, as set out in Section 5.
This Policy applies to the Creda website, the Buyer and Supplier portals, and all services provided through them.

The platform is intended for commercial businesses registered in the Kingdom, and most of its data is business data. This Policy covers the personal data of individuals associated with these businesses, including the person responsible for the account, the owner of a sole proprietorship, and the authorized signatory.
A sole proprietorship’s data is linked to its owner as a person, so we treat its financial and credit data as personal data.

This Policy does not apply to external sites and platforms you may be taken to through Creda, such as the Nafith platform for electronic promissory notes or the Moyasar payments page; each has its own privacy policy.

sections.title: Credit Score: How It Works and Who Can See It

blocks.text: 7.1 How the score is calculated

The score is built from your payment record within the platform only, and is measured from zero to one hundred. Its current factors include the share of invoices paid on time and the longest delay. Creda may develop the scoring methodology or change its factors or weights in the future; any change applies only to later calculations, and the user is notified of any material change in accordance with Section 16 of this Policy and applicable regulations.

The score is an internal indicator specific to the platform, built solely on your payment record within the platform according to the factors described above. It is not linked to any central bank or credit information bureau in any country, we do not query credit data about you from any external source for the purpose of calculating the score, and we do not provide the score to any external party unless required to do so by regulations. Your address and any data other than your payment record within the platform are not part of the score.
The “confidence level” shows how much data the score is based on: low, medium or high.
The score is updated automatically when a payment is recorded or when payment is late, and we notify you when it changes.
7.2 Who can see your credit data

rows: Your credit report at any time: the score, confidence level, payment behavior, receivables, notes, and charts.
The supplier you place an order with or deal with

The score, the confidence level, the amounts you owe to that supplier alone, and the ratings written about you by other suppliers after completing their orders, in all plans. Your comprehensive credit report (payment behavior, receivables, notes and charts) is visible only to a supplier subscribed to a plan that includes it, and no supplier can see the details of your dealings with other suppliers.

The extended report, and the platform’s aggregate reports in which your business name may appear among the highest overdue amounts, receivables or score declines, for the purposes of support, compliance, auditing and oversight. Every access to the extended report and every viewing or export of reports is recorded in a log that cannot be edited.
Any party outside the platform, such as banks, financing entities and credit bureaus
We do not share your score or report with them, and the score is not linked to any credit record outside the platform. No future sharing will take place without your separate explicit consent.

blocks.text: We will notify you if we receive a request to disclose your credit data, unless the law or an order from a competent authority prevents it, or the request falls within the cases where the regulations allow handling without prior notice.
7.3 The supplier’s credit decision
The platform does not grant credit or finance purchases. The supplier decides on deferred sales, sets your credit limit and payment period, and decides whether to require a promissory note.

A supplier may set rules that apply automatically when you place your order, such as requiring a promissory note if the score falls below a certain level, or if your outstanding amounts with it plus the value of the new order exceed your credit limit. We notify you immediately when any rule applies, and you can contact the supplier or the support team with questions.
7.4 Correcting the record

If you believe a payment was recorded incorrectly, you can submit a dispute about it from the platform. If you paid and the supplier did not record it, contact the supplier or open a support request. When the error is confirmed, the record is corrected and the score is recalculated. Disputes are subject to the time limit and procedures set out in the Terms of Use, without preventing the correction of a material error later proven by acceptable documents.
7.5 Withdrawing consent to credit processing

You can withdraw your consent to credit processing at any time, which stops the calculation of the score and its display to suppliers. Suppliers may then be unable to sell to you on deferred terms, while purchasing with immediate payment remains available. Withdrawing consent does not affect processing that took place before it, nor records we are required by regulations to retain.
We do not sell your personal data, and we share it only to the extent necessary with the following parties:

items: The other party in your dealings: the supplier sees your business name, contact details, delivery city and the order details. The buyer sees the supplier’s public profile and the pickup address when it chooses pickup. The supplier’s national address is not shown in its public profile.

Other users within defined limits: buyers in the supplier’s service areas see its public profile and the ratings it has received; the public profile includes the contact details the supplier enters, including the name of the responsible person, mobile number, email address and WhatsApp number if provided. The supplier sees the name of the buyer who wrote a rating about it. When reviewing a buyer’s orders, suppliers see the ratings written about the buyer by other suppliers.

The authorized platform administration team: it sees account data, verification documents and aggregate reports to the extent required by verification, support, oversight and auditing tasks, and access to ID images, bank details and the extended report is logged. After verifying the identity of the requester and their capacity in the business, the team may edit contact details or start a password reset procedure for support purposes. The team cannot see the current password, and every action is recorded in the account log.

Service providers we rely on to operate the platform: the cloud hosting provider, the SMS provider, the email provider, Moyasar, which handles online payment of subscription fees without card data passing through the platform, business data verification bodies, and the development and technical maintenance provider. They work under contracts that require them to maintain confidentiality, protect the data and not use it for anything other than the specified purpose.
Government and judicial authorities: whenever we are required to by applicable regulations.

The party to which ownership or operation of the platform may pass: data, rights and obligations related to the platform may be transferred in the event of a merger, acquisition, restructuring, or transfer of ownership or operation of the platform, provided that the party receiving ownership or operation complies with the data protection obligations and that users are notified as required by applicable regulations.

Promissory notes: you issue the note yourself through the Nafith platform and then upload its number and copy to Creda. Creda does not exchange data with that platform, and only the relevant supplier and the authorized administration team can see the note.

blocks.text: The platform is hosted and your data is stored on Amazon Web Services servers in a data center outside the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, in the state of Virginia in the United States. The servers meet internationally recognized security standards, and are accessed only by the operations and technical support team and the service providers we work with, each within the limits of its task.

This transfer is carried out in accordance with the legal provisions for transferring personal data outside the Kingdom, with the contractual safeguards necessary to protect your data at a level no lower than that provided for by the law. The platform can be accessed and used from any country. By using the platform, you acknowledge that your data is stored and processed outside the Kingdom as described in this Section.

blocks.text: After the period ends, we destroy the data by permanently deleting it from our systems, and from backups within seven days at most, or we convert it into data that identifies no one for statistical purposes. We do not destroy data linked to existing obligations or pending disputes until they end, even if its period has passed or you asked for it to be destroyed, nor data that regulations require us to retain. The audit log cannot be edited or have anything deleted from it before its period ends.
We apply organizational, administrative and technical measures to protect your data, including:

items: Encrypting data in transit between you and the platform.
Encrypting data while stored on servers and in the database.
A daily backup of the database.
Granting access permissions by role, so that each user sees only what their role requires.
Verification with a one-time code at registration and when changing the mobile number or email address.
Not collecting or storing bank card data ourselves, as online payment is handled by Moyasar.
Keeping an audit log that cannot be edited for financial and credit operations and administrative actions.

blocks.text: If your data is leaked, damaged or accessed unlawfully in a way that may harm you or affect your rights, we notify the competent authority within seventy-two hours of becoming aware of it, and we notify you without undue delay of what happened, the measures we took, and what you can do to protect your account.
You are also responsible for protecting your account, so do not share your password or verification code with anyone.

blocks.text: How to exercise your rights: write to us at private@creda.sa, or open a support request from the platform under the account issues category. We may ask for proof of your identity or your capacity in the business before carrying out the request. We respond to your request within thirty days, and this period may be extended by an equal period if the request requires disproportionate effort, and we will tell you the reason for the extension.

We send you in-platform notifications and SMS messages related to your account, orders, payment due dates and credit score, and we may email you about your account matters, such as activating it. These notifications are part of the service, and the essential ones cannot be turned off while your account is active.
We send you marketing messages only with your prior consent, and you can unsubscribe from them at any time from your account settings or from the link attached to each message.

We use only cookies necessary to operate the platform, such as keeping the login session, the “remember me” option and the selected language. We do not use advertising or tracking cookies. If we add analytics cookies in the future, we will request your consent in advance.
The platform is intended for commercial businesses and is used by their adult representatives, and we do not knowingly collect data from anyone under eighteen.

We may update this Policy when our services or legal requirements change. For any material change, we notify you through the platform or by email at least fifteen days before it takes effect, and we ask for your consent again where required. The date of the last update appears at the top of this Policy.

Any change that must be applied immediately to comply with a legal requirement, to address a security risk or fraud, or to protect the platform, its users or the continuity of the service is exempt from the notice period, provided that notice is given as soon as possible. This exception does not apply to any change that requires the user’s consent under applicable regulations.
This Policy is available in Arabic and English, and the Arabic text prevails in case of any discrepancy between them.
